text:
Dallas keeps handing Esa Lindell more of the game. He's averaging 22.89 minutes a night, and lately it's been more: over 24 in each of his last five, including 27.2 in Saturday's win over Buffalo. He has 1 point in 14 games, and nobody in Dallas will lose sleep over it.

That's because the job is the other end. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 9th of 215 defensemen with 500-plus minutes, worth 2.9 wins above replacement, most of it from defense at even strength, and in the 96th percentile at taking chances away. This season the Stars have had 52.2% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about the same as without him, while he soaks up the hard minutes and 32 blocked shots. The one soft spot is moving the puck out: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had only 30% of his exits keeping possession last season, so watch for clears off the glass when the forecheck comes. A third-round pick in 2012, he has spent his whole career, 780 games and counting, in Dallas.
headline: Lindell's minutes keep climbing, and the points don't matter
